data.title: Choose the sentence that uses the word correctly.

sections.question: ambitious
sections.summary: Having a strong desire to succeed, achieve something great, or reach a high level of success.

senses.definition: having a strong wish to be successful, powerful or rich
examples: She is extremely ambitious and plans to become a surgeon before the age of thirty-five.

senses.definition: (of a plan or idea) needing a great amount of effort, skill or resources to succeed
examples: The school set an ambitious target of improving exam results by twenty percent within two years.

answers.answer: She is extremely ambitious and hopes to run her own company before the age of thirty.
He was very ambitious to reach the book on the top shelf, so he stood on a chair.
She felt ambitious after the large meal and decided to take a short nap.
The ambitious storm caused serious damage to buildings across the whole city.

sections.question: confident
sections.summary: Feeling sure about your own abilities or that something will happen in the way you expect; showing a belief in yourself.

senses.definition: feeling sure about your own abilities or that something will happen as you expect
examples: She felt confident about the interview after preparing thoroughly for two weeks.

senses.definition: showing a belief in your own abilities in a way that others can see
examples: He gave a confident speech in front of the entire school without using any notes.

answers.answer: She felt confident about her presentation after practising it more than ten times.
He was very confident in his bag, which contained everything he needed for class.
She was very confident the exercise after completing it several times in a row.
The confident rain made the afternoon school sports day much more enjoyable for everyone.

sections.question: curious
sections.summary: Wanting to know or learn about something; also used to describe something that is strange or unusual.

senses.definition: wanting to know or learn about something
examples: She was curious about how the engine worked and asked the mechanic many detailed questions.

senses.definition: strange or unusual in a way that attracts your interest
examples: It is a curious fact that the building was never officially given a name.

answers.answer: The children were curious about the fossils and asked the guide question after question.
She was curious to finish the exam as quickly as possible and leave the hall early.
He felt very curious after the long run and needed a large glass of water immediately.
The student was curious the correct answer, so he looked it up in his textbook.

sections.question: efficient
sections.summary: Working well and producing good results without wasting time, money or energy.

senses.definition: working well and producing good results without wasting time, money or effort
examples: The new online booking system is far more efficient and saves staff several hours each week.

senses.definition: (of a person) able to do tasks quickly and well without wasting effort
examples: She is a very efficient worker who always meets her deadlines well ahead of time.

answers.answer: The new filing system is far more efficient and saves the team at least two hours a day.
She was so efficient by the long journey that she fell asleep before the train arrived.
He was very efficient about hearing the final exam results and could not sleep at all.
The students felt efficient after hearing that the difficult test had been cancelled.

sections.question: enthusiastic
sections.summary: Showing a lot of excitement, energy and interest about something.

senses.definition: showing a lot of interest and excitement about something
examples: The students were enthusiastic about the school trip and talked about it all week.

answers.answer: The new teacher was enthusiastic about the subject and made every lesson interesting.
She was very enthusiastic after the long exam and needed to sit quietly for a while.
He felt enthusiastic in his stomach just before giving his first public speech.
She was enthusiastic with the food at the canteen and ate it very slowly.

sections.question: independent
sections.summary: Not needing others for support; able to think or act for yourself without being controlled by others.

senses.definition: not needing other people's help or support; able to do things for yourself
examples: She is a very independent student who rarely needs guidance from the teacher.

senses.definition: not controlled or influenced by another person or group
examples: The report was carried out by an independent team of researchers with no connection to the company.

answers.answer: Living abroad taught her to be more independent and solve problems on her own.
He felt very independent after the large meal and wanted to lie down on the sofa.
The teacher was independent to explain the problem because the students did not follow.
She was independent the homework and placed it carefully on the teacher's desk.

sections.question: patient
sections.summary: Able to wait for a long time or accept problems without becoming annoyed or anxious; also a noun meaning a person receiving medical treatment.

senses.definition: able to wait for a long time or deal with a difficult situation without becoming angry or upset
examples: You need to be patient when learning a new language — real progress takes months of practice.

senses.definition: a person who is receiving medical treatment from a doctor or in a hospital
examples: The doctor visited each patient on the ward before the end of her shift.

answers.answer: The teacher was very patient with the students who found the grammar exercise difficult.
She was very patient to start the exam as soon as the papers were handed out.
He was patient in the library, borrowing four books on the topic of climate change.
She was patient the test papers from the students at the end of the lesson.

sections.question: resilient
sections.summary: Able to recover quickly from difficult situations, problems or setbacks; strong enough to return to a normal state after difficulties.

senses.definition: able to recover quickly from difficult events or situations
examples: Despite several serious setbacks, she remained resilient and never gave up on her studies.

senses.definition: (of a substance or material) able to return to its original shape after being bent or stretched
examples: The material is resilient enough to withstand extreme temperatures without breaking.

answers.answer: She was resilient throughout the difficult year and managed to pass all her exams.
He was very resilient after the class and asked the teacher many more questions.
She felt resilient to start the new chapter without finishing the previous one first.
The resilient weather forced the school to cancel all outdoor activities that afternoon.

sections.question: successful
sections.summary: Having achieved what you wanted to achieve; producing good results or being popular.

senses.definition: having achieved an aim or reached a desired result
examples: The fundraising event was very successful and raised over five thousand pounds for charity.

senses.definition: (of a person) having become rich or well-known through work or effort
examples: She became a successful architect after graduating at the top of her class.

answers.answer: The school's new reading programme was very successful, with results improving across all year groups.
She was very successful that the difficult exam had been postponed until the following week.
He was successful to pass the driving test first time, which surprised him greatly.
The successful student left the classroom and walked quietly to the school library.

sections.question: supportive
sections.summary: Giving help, encouragement or sympathy to someone, especially during a difficult time.

senses.definition: giving help and encouragement to someone, especially during a difficult time
examples: Her colleagues were very supportive during her illness and helped cover her workload.

answers.answer: Her friends were incredibly supportive during the difficult period and checked on her every day.
He was very supportive of money and put a small amount in a savings account every month.
She felt very supportive after receiving the unexpected good news from the admissions office.
The supportive rain fell throughout the night and watered the farmers' fields perfectly.
